description: We are a dedicated team driven by a passion for aerospace engineering, computational mechanics, and space exploration. Based out of the Madras Institute of Technology, our core expertise lies in aerodynamics, propulsion, and advanced aerospace design. We combine rigorous analytical problem-solving with practical software capabilities to conceptualize and build innovative solutions for complex space and earth challenges.
summary:
ARES-X Mars Mission Studio v4.0 is a browser-based educational application developed using HTML, CSS, JavaScript and Three.js. It allows users to design and simulate three types of Mars spacecraft: Orbiter, Lander and Rover.

The application provides a step-by-step design studio where users can customize spacecraft components, select scientific instruments, configure power and propulsion systems, and choose mission parameters. Its interactive 3D CAD viewport updates in real time, offering different visualization modes.

ARES-X also includes an engineering evaluation system that checks spacecraft mass, cost, power requirements and compatibility. A telemetry dashboard displays mission performance, while dedicated simulations demonstrate the major stages of each spacecraft's mission. Users can generate and download mission reports.

The project aims to make Mars exploration and spacecraft engineering easier to understand through an engaging, interactive experience. It uses simplified calculations for educational purposes rather than real-world engineering analysis.
details: ARES-X: Mars Mission Studio ARES-X is an interactive, browser-based platform that allows users to design spacecraft and explore the challenges of planning a mission to Mars. Users can choose between three spacecraft types: Orbiter, Lander and Rover, and customize each one through a step-by-step design process covering mission objectives, structure, power systems, propulsion, communication, scientific instruments and engineering limits. As users make their choices, the 3D spacecraft model updates in real time. They can explore their designs using different viewing modes, including solid, exploded and X-ray views. The application also features a live telemetry dashboard that tracks important values such as spacecraft mass, estimated cost and power balance. Once the design is complete, the engineering evaluation system identifies potential problems and checks whether the spacecraft meets the required limits. Users can then run a mission simulation to see how their spacecraft performs and generate a downloadable mission report. Benefits and Intended Impact ARES-X makes the complex concepts of spacecraft engineering easier to understand through hands-on learning. It helps students explore how mass, power, cost and scientific objectives influence mission planning. Since it runs directly in a web browser without installation, it can be used by students, educators and space enthusiasts as an accessible learning tool. Tools and Technologies Used The project is developed using HTML5, CSS3 and JavaScript, with Three.js (r128) powering the interactive 3D spacecraft models. HTML Canvas is used for visual elements such as the animated starfield and telemetry charts. The application is designed as a single-page web application without requiring a backend server. Creativity and Innovation The main idea behind ARES-X is to turn spacecraft engineering into an interactive learning experience. Instead of simply reading about Mars missions, users can make their own design decisions and see how those choices affect mission performance. If a mission fails, the application highlights the engineering issues responsible for the failure, helping users learn through experimentation. Factors Considered During development, we focused on important spacecraft engineering constraints, including mass limits, mission budgets, power requirements and compatibility between different subsystems. We also considered ease of use, browser performance, interactive visualization and clear feedback to make the experience accessible to beginners while still introducing meaningful engineering concepts.
